# Quantum Hadamard Powers

> Heralded normalized coordinatewise powers of an unknown quantum state from reversible state preparation, with instance-sensitive source-query bounds and a matched classical benchmark for the measured square law.

- [Overview and reading routes](README.md)
- [Input contract, target state, trace error and query theorems](science/model.md)
- [Exact coherent collision extraction, multiplicities and residual factorization](science/extraction.md)
- [Local-projector encoding, tilted spectral filter and unknown-moment schedule](science/spectral.md)
- [Clean Haar lower bound, matched evaluator and classical birthday algorithm](science/benchmarks.md)
- [Routing, occupancy work, source costs, width and crossover](science/resources.md)
- [Previous results and source attribution](references/RELATED_WORK.md)

## Reading choices

- For the story, read the overview, extraction and benchmarks.
- For the theorem, read the model, extraction and spectral filter in order.
- For implementation choices, read the spectral filter and resource account together.
- For self-directed study, use the bridge beside the milestone map.

## Scope of the claims

- A clean source yields a coherent powered state. A source with garbage yields a purification sufficient to sample the powered probabilities.
- The earlier collective extraction is exact on its ideal success branch. Finite spectral filtering contributes the stated approximation error.
- The unknown-moment instance bound is expected query cost. The dimension-based bound gives a hard budget with the residual failure probability included in the accuracy guarantee.
- The evaluator lower bound applies to the measured square law. The separate Haar-state lower bound applies to coherent squared-state preparation.
- Oracle query savings do not give a gate-time claim without a source-cost and routing comparison.
